Events at London Business School
Terms & Conditions
The terms and conditions provide guidance to event organiser(s) on the process to be followed when organising any event on campus. They apply to events organised by students and staff alike.
It also includes a description of the responsibilities that the event organiser(s) assumes when organising an event.
Your starting point should always be to secure the correct space for your event. Do not publicise your event until your space is confirmed.
Requests for space and associated services submitted less than two weeks in advance may prove difficult for service teams to accommodate. If your event will be taking place in less than two weeks’ time, you must provide details of all anticipated requirements at the time of making your space enquiry. The Space Management team will then check with the service delivery teams to see if the services you have requested are possible.
Details of logistical requirements must be submitted to the appropriate service delivery teams by the stated deadline.
Space Booking
All event organiser(s) must book event spaces through the Space Management team (space@london.edu).

The Space Management team will liaise with the event organiser(s) to identify the most appropriate space on Campus for the event. This should be done as far in advance as possible and before speakers are confirmed. The Space Management team cannot guarantee that appropriate spaces will be available at short notice.
The Space Management team will hold the agreed space on a provisional basis and confirm this to the event organiser(s) by email.
Named Point of Contact
The event organiser(s) must oversee the management of the event and act as the point of contact for all school departments.
The number of person(s) required to oversee an event will depend on the size of the event. All person(s) overseeing an event are jointly accountable for compliance to this policy. NB: Names and contact details must be provided when completing the events form.

For student-run events, a nominated person, who is overseeing the organisation of the event, must sign these terms and conditions in order for the event to proceed.

For staff-run events, it is assumed that the terms and conditions for running events at the School have been accepted.
Catering and Alcohol
All catering is provided by the in-house catering service (Lexington).  They should be emailed with your requirements for a quote. (cateringevents@london.edu)
Catering bookings orders are to be placed 30 days before the event and final catering numbers need to be confirmed 5 days before the event. If these timescales are not met it may not be possible to provide or fulfil the catering requirements.
External Catering Provision for your event: all catering on School premises is contracted out to our catering provider and as such there are strict policy guidelines regarding external catering being brought onto campus for a managed event. This includes food supplied by an external catering company, restaurant or fast-food outlet.
LBS’ contract catering supplier ensures that all food hygiene, allergen controls and health and safety regulatory processes are followed to safeguard our community. Before you consider using an external catering supplier you must apply for the necessary approval by contacting cateringevents@london.edu.
Alcohol can only be consumed in certain areas of campus and must be ordered via Catering (cateringevents@london.edu).

Alcohol may only be served by Catering Staff or by the Sundowners crew under the supervision of an approved Personal Licence holder. There are strict laws which govern the provision of alcohol. Failure to comply with these leaves the School liable for prosecution.
Access to the bar area in the Nash Lounge is at the discretion of the Catering General Manager
The use of Sundowners crew and equipment to serve alcohol is at the discretion of the Sundowners Chief
Please note - as there is little hospitality/function space at Sammy Ofer Centre, only limited catering options are available.
Security
Additional Security will be required for larger events (100+) and the number of security officers will be determined by a risk assessment carried out by the Head of Security. Please inform security@london.edu no later than 3 weeks before the start of the event.
The event organiser(s) is responsible for ensuring that guest numbers do not exceed those stated.
For higher risk events (50+ plus persons, alcohol served) a procedure is to be agreed as to how numbers will be managed, i.e. wristbands and this must be agreed by Head of Security.

Tickets: a maximum number of tickets will be set for each event space (e.g. 300 for Nash Lounge) which may be sold; tickets must not be sold on the night for higher risk events. Notification of this must also be sent to attendees by event organiser(s) prior to event.
Contact details for the event organiser(s) must be given to Security and the organiser must remain contactable during whole course of the event.
Decorations
The nominated event organiser(s) is responsible for ensuring that decorations for the event will not damage paintwork, artwork, fixtures and fittings and must be discussed at the event planning stage. Only decorations approved in advance will be permitted.
The preferred form of decoration is helium balloons and/or lighting that will not damage the décor.
Decorations may only be attached with masking tape or blu tack. The use of sellotape, pins, nails, and parcel tape are not permitted.
The event organiser(s) will be responsible for removing all decorations and fixings at the end of the event and reporting any damage or additional cleaning required.
The event organiser(s) will be responsible for making good the cost of repair or redecoration due to damage. These costs will be taken directly from the event organiser(s) budget code.

Noise and Damage
The event organiser(s) is responsible for ensuring that the event does not impinge on other users of school facilities e.g. noise, unruly behaviour.
The event organiser(s) is responsible for ensuring that there is no damage to the furniture and/or fixtures by their guests on campus.
The event organiser(s) will be responsible for making good the cost of repair or replacement to any damage. These costs will be taken directly from the event organiser(s) budget code.
Cleaning
Events may be subject to a cleaning charge when food and/or alcohol are served.  This will be determined via an independent assessment of the cleaning requirements by the Cleaning Manager prior to the event and may be charged accordingly.
A quote will be returned to the event organiser within three working days of submission of the logistics form.
Any cleaning required over and above that which has been paid for (e.g. extensive staining to carpets/walls etc.) will be at an additional charge.
Non-compliance with terms and conditions for Student Clubs (agreed with Student Association)
Any student clubs that do not comply with this policy will be subject to punitive measures that could include:

Smaller budget allocations in following academic year
Loss of rights to organise events in the current academic year
This will be a joint decision between the Head of Customer Experience, Associate Director of Estates and Campus Services, General Catering Manager and the nominated Senior Campus Operations Officer(s).
